profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting for an updated systematic review in clinical machine learning. Context: a faculty-led ML research group wants to extend a prior review on deep learning for temporal data representation in structured electronic health records from the original cutoff of August 30, 2020 through the present, and package it as a reproducible review protocol plus a manuscript draft for a medical informatics journal submission. Agenda: confirm the practical inclusion boundary, decide how to reuse the prior search and hand-search process, define the extraction template for challenges and methods, and split responsibilities for search, screening, and coding. Expected outcome: a shared plan for the search workflow, screening setup, coding template, and a two-week timeline for pilot screening and protocol drafting.

members.name: Dr. Lena Park
members.expertise: Clinical machine learning, longitudinal EHR modeling, evidence synthesis for informatics
members.background: Leads a hospital-affiliated ML lab and previously co-authored a review on deep learning methods for temporal EHR data; experienced in framing broad research syntheses that support grants and perspective pieces.
members.private_state: Wants a fast, low-friction update that can feed an upcoming grant renewal and prefers to preserve continuity with the earlier review rather than redesign the protocol from scratch.
hidden_assumptions: A 'temporal representation' paper includes any deep learning study that models longitudinal structured EHR sequences for prediction, even if the representation is only an internal intermediate and not the paper's headline contribution.
A study still counts as 'structured EHR' if its main longitudinal signal is coded events, labs, medications, or vitals, even when it adds side information from notes or images.
When someone says 'the conference list from last time,' they mean the set of hand-searched venues documented in the appendix and notes from the original published review.
A paper should be coded as addressing irregularity, heterogeneity, sparsity, or opacity only when the authors explicitly frame the method as tackling that challenge.

members.name: Rahul Mehta
members.expertise: Representation learning for clinical time series, systematic review workflows, reproducible literature mining
members.background: Recently finished a PhD on sequence modeling for EHRs and has been maintaining the lab's Zotero libraries and screening templates for several informatics reviews.
members.private_state: Wants the project to become a standalone, methodologically clean review that will be publishable in its own right, and is quietly worried that a broad protocol will create inconsistent screening and extraction work.
hidden_assumptions: A 'temporal representation' paper should have representation learning or sequence encoding itself as a central methodological contribution, not merely use a standard deep model inside a downstream prediction pipeline.
To remain comparable and easy to code, 'structured EHR' excludes studies that incorporate free text, imaging, or other unstructured modalities, even if structured temporal data are also present.
When someone says 'the conference list from last time,' they mean the lab's more recent Zotero proceedings set used for internal scoping, which emphasizes AMIA, IEEE BHI, and MLHC-type venues.

A paper can be coded as addressing irregularity, heterogeneity, sparsity, or opacity whenever the architecture operationally handles that issue, even if the authors never name the challenge explicitly.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a temporal representation paper
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to include papers on 'temporal data representation' in EHRs.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means any deep model over longitudinal structured EHR data where patient state is represented internally for a prediction or risk modeling task.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means papers whose main methodological contribution is the representation scheme itself, such as visit embeddings, sequence encoders, temporal abstraction layers, or learned patient states discussed as the contribution.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both meanings sound fully compatible with the review title and prior literature, and neither side expects that such a familiar phrase needs narrowing during a high-level planning meeting.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to focus on 'structured EHR data.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes mixed-modality studies remain in scope if the backbone is longitudinal coded EHR data and unstructured notes or images are only auxiliary inputs.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes any use of unstructured modalities puts the paper out of scope because the review is supposed to isolate methods for structured temporal EHR alone.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'structured EHR' feels standard and already settled by the seed topic, so both treat edge-case multimodal papers as obvious rather than something requiring explicit boundary-setting.

misalignment_points.topic: Which hand-search venue set to reuse
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'reuse the conference list from last time' for hand-searching.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the conference and proceedings list attached to the earlier published review and its supporting notes.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the lab's later Zotero proceedings collection from an internal 2023 scoping exercise, which overlaps partially but not completely with the earlier published list.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both sources are genuinely 'the list from last time' from their own vantage point, and because hand-searching is a secondary search component, the phrase sounds operationally routine rather than decision-critical.

misalignment_points.topic: How to tag which challenge a paper addresses
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to code the 'challenge addressed' using the prior categories of irregularity, heterogeneity, sparsity, and opacity.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes a paper counts for a challenge only if the authors explicitly motivate, discuss, or evaluate the method in relation to that challenge.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes a paper counts whenever the method functionally addresses the challenge, such as a masking or time-gap mechanism implying irregularity handling even without explicit author language.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both think they are merely preserving the earlier taxonomy, and the disagreement is about the evidentiary threshold for coding rather than the taxonomy labels themselves, so the surface agreement feels complete.

If we keep continuity with the published framing on deep learning for temporal EHR representation and just move the date range from the August 2020 cutoff forward, I can use the update for the grant renewal and maybe a perspective-style synthesis. Rahul is strong on workflow, so if I frame this as an update with a quick protocol draft, we can keep momentum and avoid getting bogged down in methodological debates.

My main goal is pretty simple: update the earlier review on deep learning for temporal data representation in structured electronic health records from the 2020 cutoff up through now, and get a protocol draft moving quickly so we have something usable within the next couple of weeks.

If we anchor it around temporal representation in structured EHRs and tighten the workflow, I can make this reproducible enough to stand on its own later. I need to avoid a vague screen that pulls in every prediction paper with an RNN buried inside it or mixed-modality studies that will be messy to code. But at this level, saying we keep the same overall inclusion logic should reassure her.
turns.utterance: I think the easiest path is to preserve the same overall inclusion logic around temporal representation in structured EHRs and just modernize the search window and workflow. That should keep it comparable while still making the update cleaner operationally.

turns.inner_thought: Good. I'll keep the taxonomy but make the coding sheet a bit more structured than before. turns.inner_thought: We should sanity-check a few edge cases early, especially papers that are clearly grounded in longitudinal coded EHR but bring in some side information.
